reference: Installed GNU coreutils command-line tools selected by each parity case, executed by the harness reference Bash. Seeded shuffle is only compared on a zero-count/single-item boundary because this loadable documents a different random-source algorithm from GNU.
coverage: Bash type/help metadata contract for the dispatcher
tac with overlapping literal and NUL separators over private binary fixtures
factor multiple operands; fmt paragraph wrapping; tsort on a uniquely ordered chain
nproc OpenMP cap and ignore option with fixed environment values
numfmt IEC conversion in both directions
shuf zero-count and singleton range boundaries
install content, exact modes, and parent directory creation in the private tree
mknod FIFO creation and shred zero-fill/unlink on private relative files
Private FIFO default/explicit modes across umasks, existing-entry preservation, and restored masks after errors.
numfmt GNU options: --suffix, --padding, --field, --format, --round, --header, --from/--to-unit, --invalid modes, -d and option/conversion diagnostics (guest pass 2 G27)
exclusions: Shuf permutation distribution and seeded output are not GNU byte-parity claims because the documented implementation uses a different random-source algorithm.
Character and block device creation is deferred because the harness removes capabilities and has no device-node mock; physical shred erasure is not established by regular-file fixtures.
The suite does not exercise yes's unbounded output, groups, or every unsupported GNU option.

cases.purpose: Bash metadata must identify coreutils as a builtin and resolve its attached help text without invoking a dispatcher verb.
cases.script: [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]] || exit 1; help coreutils > metadata.out; printf 'metadata ok\n'

cases.purpose: Reverse records using an overlapping multi-byte literal separator and the documented empty-separator NUL mode, preserving binary bytes and unterminated tails.
cases.script: cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; printf 'A::B:::tail' > overlap; printf 'left\000middle\000last' > nul-records; cu tac --separator='::' overlap; cu tac -s '' nul-records

cases.purpose: Check exact GNU factor formatting across unity, composites and a prime, then verify the malformed-operand error after successful operands.
cases.script: cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; cu factor 1 84 360 99991; cu factor not-a-number

cases.purpose: Check word wrapping at a narrow explicit width and preservation of a paragraph boundary.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; printf 'alpha beta gamma

zulu
' | cu fmt -w 5

cases.purpose: Check topological ordering where the input graph has one required order, avoiding unspecified tie ordering.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; printf 'a b
b c
c d
' | cu tsort

cases.purpose: With fixed OpenMP environment values, verify GNU's thread-limit cap and ignore subtraction without depending on host CPU count.
cases.script: cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; export OMP_NUM_THREADS=5 OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=2; cu nproc --ignore=1

cases.purpose: Compare IEC human-readable output and IEC suffix parsing over exact integral values.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; printf '1024
1536
' | cu numfmt --to=iec; printf '1K
1.5K
' | cu numfmt --from=iec

cases.purpose: Check GNU-compatible zero-output count and singleton integer range boundaries; this deliberately does not assert a random permutation.
cases.script: cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; printf 'seeddata' > seed; cu shuf --random-source=seed -n 0 -i 1-10; cu shuf --random-source=seed -n 1 -i 7-7

cases.purpose: Verify regular-file replacement copies binary content with an exact requested mode, -D creates relative parent directories, and -d creates a directory with an exact mode.
cases.script: cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; printf 'blob\000tail\n' > source; printf 'old contents\n' > installed; cu install -m 0640 source installed; cu install -D -m 0751 source nested/deep/copied; cu install -d -m 0700 local/state

cases.purpose: Create a FIFO under a relative private path with an explicit mode and compare its type and exact mode with GNU mknod.
cases.script: cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; cu mknod -m 0620 pipe p

cases.purpose: Exercise the explicit zero-fill pass and unlink behavior only on a small generated private fixture; the tree comparison verifies removal.
cases.script: cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; printf 'fixture secret\000bytes\n' > private-file; cu shred -n 0 -z -u private-file

cases.purpose: Cover the loadable's character and block device-node operations when a safe privileged fixture becomes available.
cases.reason: Character/block node creation needs a disposable VM or a reviewed mknod syscall mock with synthetic major/minor numbers. A future case should verify node type, mode, device numbers, existing-path behavior, and the expected permission-denied path. The current capability-free fixture covers FIFO creation only.

cases.purpose: Private FIFO defaults respect umask; explicit modes override it, and later file creation proves the caller mask was restored. No device nodes are created.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; for mask in 000 022 077; do
 (umask "$mask"; cu mknod "pipe-$mask" p; cu mknod -m 0620 "explicit-$mask" p; : > "after-$mask")
done

cases.purpose: Existing and missing-parent FIFO failures preserve the existing node mode and restore umask before subsequent private file creation.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; umask 077
before=$(umask)
cu mknod -m 0640 existing p
rc=0; cu mknod -m 0666 existing p || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
rc=0; cu mknod -m 0666 absent/pipe p || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 && $(umask) == "$before" ]]
: > after
printf "preserved\n"

cases.purpose: The dispatcher rereads a fresh redirected stream in the same shell on each call, preserving binary record tails.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }
printf 'one\ntwo\000tail' > input
cu tac < input
cu tac < input
cu tac < input

cases.purpose: Compare GNU shred -x exact-size zero overwrite and retain any unsupported-option difference. This compatibility check is separate from supported -s size behavior and does not establish physical erasure.
A supported explicit size overwrites twelve bytes of a small private file with zeros; retain and compare the complete resulting artifact.
Apply --suffix, --padding (both alignments), --format width/zero/precision/prefix text, every --round method and --to-unit/--from-unit scaling instead of printing a stray 0 (guest pass 2 G27).
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }
cu numfmt --to=iec --suffix=B 1024
cu numfmt --from=iec --suffix=B 1KB
cu numfmt --padding=8 1024; cu numfmt --padding=-8 1024 | od -c
cu numfmt --format=%04f 1; cu numfmt --format='x%08.2fy' 3.14159; cu numfmt --format='%08.1f' --to=iec 1500
for r in up down from-zero towards-zero nearest; do cu numfmt --to=iec --round=$r 1025 1500 1075; done
cu numfmt --to=si --format=%.3f 1234567; cu numfmt --to=iec-i --padding=10 --suffix=B 1048576
cu numfmt --to=iec --from-unit=512 4; cu numfmt --to-unit=1K 4096; cu numfmt --from-unit=1Ki 1
cu numfmt 1.5 1.50 .5 -- -.5; cu numfmt --to=iec 1.5 2.5 9.95 999 1023 1000000
cu numfmt --from=auto 1Ki 1K 1Mi

cases.purpose: Convert only the --field selection (lists, ranges, custom -d delimiter, auto-padding of blank-separated fields) and pass --header lines through untouched.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }
printf 'a 2048\n' | cu numfmt --field=2 --to=iec
printf 'H\n1024\n' | cu numfmt --header --to=iec
printf 'H1\nH2\n1024\n' | cu numfmt --header=2 --to=iec
cu numfmt -d: --field=2 --to=iec 'a:2048:3'
cu numfmt --field=2-3 --to=iec 'a 2048 4096 x'
cu numfmt --field=- --to=iec '1024 2048'; cu numfmt --field=1,3 --to=iec '1024 2048 4096'
cu numfmt --field 2 --to iec 'a  2048'; cu numfmt --to=iec '  1024'; cu numfmt ' 12 '
printf 'total 0\n-rw-r--r-- 1 u g 123456 Jan 1 x\n' | cu numfmt --header --field 5 --to=iec

cases.purpose: Invalid numbers and rejected suffixes print a diagnostic and exit 2 without a stray 0: abort stops at the first error, fail/warn/ignore keep the original text with their own statuses.
Option errors exit 1 with GNU's checks: unknown options, invalid --to/--round arguments, padding 0, bad --format, field lists, delimiter length and --grouping conflicts.
install -t DIR and --target-directory=DIR copy every source into DIR with the requested mode; -D -t creates DIR; -T installs onto the exact name; -c is accepted (guest pass 2 G35).
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }
umask 022
printf 'x\n' > s; printf 'y\n' > s2; mkdir D E
cu install -m 755 -t D s s2
cu install -m 640 --target-directory=E s
cu install -D -t new/sub s
cu install -T s exact
cu install -c -m 600 s2 copied
stat -c '%n %a' D/s D/s2 E/s new/sub/s exact copied

cases.purpose: -t on a missing or non-directory target fails with status 1; -t with -T is rejected; -T refuses an existing directory and extra operands.

shred -v reports each pass (random, then 000000 for -z) on stderr; --remove=unlink, --remove=wipe and -u report removing / renamed to / removed, wipe renames through shorter all-'0' names and skips names in use (guest pass 3, G53). -x keeps the fixture size: without it GNU rounds the overwrite up to a whole block, which this shred does not do.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }
printf 'data\n' > f; cu shred -v -x -n 2 -z f 2>&1
printf 'x\n' > abc; cu shred -v --remove=wipe -n 1 abc 2>&1; [[ -e abc ]] || echo gone
printf 'x\n' > g; : > 0; cu shred -vu -n1 g 2>&1; [[ -e 1 ]] || echo no-1
printf 'x\n' > h; cu shred --remove=unlink -v --iterations=1 h 2>&1
printf 'x\n' > k; cu shred --zero -n 0 --remove k; [[ -e k ]] || echo k-gone
cu shred -u -n 1 nofile 2>/dev/null || echo rc=$?
cu shred --remove=bad k 2>/dev/null || echo bad-rejected

cases.purpose: Guest pass 4 G68: fmt -u/--uniform-spacing puts one space between words and two after a sentence end; without -u, fmt keeps the input's inter-word spacing (GNU), where bash-os used to collapse it.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }
printf 'a   b.    c
' | cu fmt -u
printf 'a   b.    c
' | cu fmt
printf 'One.  Two three.
Four   five
' | cu fmt --uniform-spacing -w 12
printf 'x  y
' | cu fmt -su

cases.purpose: Guest pass 4 G68: fmt -p/--prefix STRING refills only lines that start with STRING (after optional indentation), reattaches the prefix, and copies every other line unchanged.

fmt joins only lines of equal indentation, re-introduces tabs, honours -c/-t/-g, never lets a line reach the -w width, and handles old -WIDTH syntax, options after operands and its option errors as GNU fmt does.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }
s() { local rc=0; "$@" || rc=$?; echo "rc=$rc"; }
printf 'a
  b
' | cu fmt
printf 'aaaa bbbb
' | cu fmt -w 9
printf '	x y
	z
' | cu fmt
printf '  first line here
second line text
third
' | cu fmt -c -w 12
printf 'tag line
    body one
    body two
' | cu fmt -t -w 15
printf 'a b c d e f
' | cu fmt -g 4
printf 'p q r s
' > in; cu fmt -5 in; cu fmt in -w 3
s cu fmt -w abc in 2>/dev/null; s cu fmt -q in 2>/dev/null; s cu fmt -w 3000 in 2>/dev/null; s cu fmt missing in 2>/dev/null

cases.purpose: Guest pass 4 G68: an odd number of tokens prints nothing and fails with status 1 (GNU: 'input contains an odd number of tokens'), also when the pairs before the lone token are valid.
Guest pass 4 G68: install -C/--compare leaves a destination with the same content, mode and owner untouched (its inode keeps a second hard link) and replaces it when the content or mode differs.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }
umask 022
printf 'x\n' > s; cu install -C s t; ln t keep
cu install -C s t; stat -c '%h %a' t
cu install --compare -m 644 s t; stat -c '%h %a' t; ln -f t keep
printf 'y\n' > s; cu install -C -m 644 s t; stat -c '%h %a' t; cat t
ln -f t keep; cu install s t; stat -c '%h' t
